quotes.text: Azure Monitor isn't a single tool. It's a platform that pulls together metrics, logs, traces, and alerts from Azure on premises and even other clouds.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Defines Azure Monitor as a platform rather than one tool.

quotes.text: Metrics tell you something is wrong, logs tell you why. Imagine driving your car. The check engine light comes on, and that's a metric telling you something is wrong right now
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Memorable analogy for the difference between metrics and logs.

quotes.text: If you're still running that old agent, your data has stopped flowing. Everyone needs to be on the Azure Monitor agent with data collection rules. If you haven't migrated yet, that's your number one priority.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters

quotes.text: The biggest mistake people make is sending everything to the analytics tier by default, tier your telemetry, not every log needs full query capabilities. Treat cheap data like cheap data.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters

quotes.text: Here's the bottom line. Monitoring becomes proactive when you set up alerts properly. You catch issues before users notice them.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Sums up the value of well-designed alerts.

chapters.title: Cost optimization and how it all fits together

takeaways: Azure Monitor is Microsoft's central observability platform: metrics tell you something is wrong, logs in a Log Analytics workspace queried with KQL tell you why.

Data flows in from Azure resources, Application Insights, the Azure Monitor Agent (also via Azure Arc), Entra ID and security tools, and is visualized in workbooks and acted on with alerts, action groups and Logic Apps.
Migrate off the retired Log Analytics agent, adopt OpenTelemetry, and control cost by tiering logs, setting per-table retention and using sampling and budget alerts.
hook: Jumping between five screens whenever something breaks? This episode explains Azure Monitor in plain English for Azure beginners and admins, covering metrics, logs, KQL, workbooks, alerts and the 2026 changes, plus practical tips to keep monitoring costs under control.
